27 The diagram shows an electron in a uniform electric field.
In which direction will the field accelerate the electron?
electron
A
electric
D
B
field
C

hints: Notice the electric field arrows in the diagram all point horizontally to the right, while arrows A and C point vertically.
Recall that field direction is defined as the force direction on a positive charge, using $F = qE$.
Consider what the negative sign of the electron charge does to the direction of $F$ compared to $E$, then compare B with the opposite horizontal direction.
walkthrough: Identify from the diagram that the uniform electric field $E$ points horizontally to the right at the position of the electron.
State the rule for electric force: $F = qE$, where the vector direction of $F$ depends on the sign of charge $q$.
Note that the electron has negative charge, so $q$ is negative and the force vector is antiparallel to the field vector.
Therefore the acceleration $a = F/m$ must also be antiparallel to $E$, so horizontally to the left.
Directions A and C can be rejected because they are perpendicular to $E$, and direction B can be rejected because it is parallel to $E$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Direction A is perpendicular to the field lines, but the electric force on a charge in a uniform field is parallel to the field lines.

B.explanation: Direction B is along the field direction, which is the force direction for a positive charge, not for the negative electron.

C.explanation: Direction C is perpendicular to the field lines, but there is no vertical component of $F = qE$ when the field is horizontal.

D.explanation: Direction D is opposite to the field arrows. Since the electron charge $q$ is negative, $F = qE$ is opposite to $E$.
